headline: The Select Board examined severe potential budget cuts ahead of a possible FY28 tax override, while boards advanced zoning changes for senior housing.
synopsis: Southborough boards began detailed reviews of FY28 operating and capital budgets amid preparations for a potential operational tax override in May 2027. Public safety and school officials warned that a level-funded budget would require eliminating police, firefighting, and teaching positions, while town capital requests exceeded available non-debt funding targets by one million dollars. Simultaneously, the Select Board and Zoning Board of Appeals reviewed zoning amendments to eliminate the municipal cap on 55-plus housing and mandate affordable units. In land use, the Planning Board reviewed site plans for the proposed Costco project and approved scenic road tree removals, while the Conservation Commission approved local trail and infrastructure work.

highlights.title: Select Board reviews FY28 departmental budgets and override risks
highlights.why: Departments presented level-service and level-funded options, warning that level funding would force cuts to police officers, firefighters, and up to 15 school staff members.

highlights.title: Select Board sponsors zoning amendment to expand senior housing
highlights.why: The board voted to sponsor a Town Meeting warrant article removing the 7 percent cap on 55-plus developments and requiring projects to include 12.5 percent affordable units.

highlights.title: Capital committee faces one million dollar funding gap
highlights.why: Town capital requests reached roughly 2.2 million dollars against a 1.2 million dollar Select Board placeholder, prompting discussions on bonding thresholds.

highlights.title: Planning Board reviews Costco lighting and landscaping plans
highlights.why: The board held technical reviews on dark-sky fixtures, plantings, and stormwater systems for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco at 21 Coslin Drive.

highlights.title: Planning Board approves tree removals on scenic roads
highlights.why: The board approved a Department of Public Works petition to remove hazardous trees along scenic roads, modifying one tree at 3 Pine Hill Road to full removal.
